Definition: probably from the base of G726; fruit (as plucked), literally or figuratively:--fruit.
BiblicalUsage: Karpos is fruit — what is plucked from the tree, whether the fruit of the vine or the fruit of the Spirit. I am the vine, ye are the branches: he that abideth in Me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit; herein is My Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; and the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe fruit is the whole test of the Christian life: not the leaves, not the talk, but the fruit — and the fruit grows only by abiding in the Vine, because a branch cut off can do nothing. I would rather bear a little fruit abiding than make a great show cut off.
RelatedTopics: Fruit of the Spirit; Vine and Branches; Growth
